chapterNote: The evening prayer of the ancient church — Vespers opened with it for centuries because of verse 2: let my prayer be set before You like incense, the lifting of my hands like the evening sacrifice. It is a prayer for a man surrounded by wickedness who is more afraid of joining it than of being hurt by it. So the petitions are about himself: set a guard over my mouth; keep the door of my lips; do not let my heart lean toward evil, or my hands practice it with the workers of iniquity, or my appetite accept their delicacies. He would rather be struck by a righteous man — that is kindness, oil on the head — than feasted by the wicked. The middle verses are the most difficult Hebrew in the Psalter, but the picture is clear enough: the wicked leaders thrown down on the rocks, bones scattered at Sheol's mouth like turned earth. And the close is the psalm's real posture: my eyes are on You, O GOD the Lord; in You I take refuge; keep me from their traps, and let the wicked fall into their own nets while I pass safely by.

1.text: A psalm of David. O LORD, I call to You — hurry to me! Give ear to my voice when I call to You.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David. LORD [YHWH], I cry [qara] unto You: make haste [chush] unto me; give ear [azan] unto my voice [qol], when I cry [qara] unto You.
1.notes: YHWH qeratikha, chushah li (H7121, H2363): I have called — hurry to me: the urgency-verb of Psalm 70:1. haazinah qoli be-qori-lakh (H238, H6963): give ear to the voice, when I call — qara twice in one verse, the evening's first act.

2.text: Let my prayer be set before You like incense, the lifting of my hands like the evening offering.
2.amp: Let my prayer [tephillah] be set forth ['directed', kun — established, arranged, the KJV margin] before [panim] You as incense [qetoreth]; and the lifting up [maseth] of my hands [kaph] as the evening [erev] sacrifice [minchah — the grain offering].
2.notes: tikkon tephillati qetoret le-phanekha (H3559, H8605, H7004, H6440): prayer arranged like incense on the altar of Exodus 30, rising — masat kappai minchat-arev (H4864, H3709, H4503, H6153): open palms as the evening minchah, the last offering of the temple day. Revelation 5:8 makes the incense the prayers of the saints; Vespers opened with this verse for a thousand years.

3.text: Set a guard over my mouth, O LORD; keep watch at the door of my lips.
3.amp: Set [shith] a watch [shomrah — a guard post], O LORD [YHWH], before my mouth [peh]; keep [natsar — guard] the door [delet] of my lips [saphah].
3.notes: shitah YHWH shomrah le-phi (H7896, H8108, H6310): station a sentry at my mouth — nitsrah al-dal sephatai (H5341, H1817, H8193): guard the DOOR of my lips, as if the mouth were a gate that needs a watchman. James 3 in a prayer: the tongue is the first thing a surrounded man asks God to hold.

4.text: Do not let my heart lean toward anything evil, to busy itself with wicked deeds alongside men who work iniquity; and do not let me eat of their delicacies.
4.amp: Incline [natah — bend, turn] not my heart [leb] to any evil [ra] thing [dabar], to practise [alal — busy oneself with] wicked [resha] works [alilah — deeds] with men [ish] that work [paal] iniquity [aven]: and let me not eat [lacham] of their dainties [manammim — delicacies].
4.notes: al-tat-libbi le-dabar ra (H5186, H3820, H1697, H7451): do not let my heart BEND — natah, the verb God uses for turning hearts — le-hitolel alilot be-resha (H5953, H5949, H7562), to get busy with wicked deeds, et-ishim poale-aven (H376, H6466, H205). u-bal-elcham be-manammehem (H3898, H4516): and no place at their table — the delicacies are the bribe, the feast that buys silence.

5.text: Let a righteous man strike me — that is covenant kindness; let him correct me — that is oil for my head, which my head will not refuse. For my prayer is still against their evil doings.
5.amp: Let the righteous [tsaddiq] smite [halam] me; it shall be a kindness [chesed — covenant love]: and let him reprove [yakach — correct] me; it shall be an excellent [rosh — chief, finest] oil [shemen], which shall not break ['let not their precious oil break my head', nu — refuse, the KJV margin] my head [rosh]: for yet my prayer [tephillah] also shall be in their calamities [ra — evil deeds].
5.notes: yehelmeni tsaddiq chesed (H1986, H6662, H2617): a righteous man's blow is CHESED — Proverbs 27:6's faithful wounds — ve-yokhicheni shemen rosh (H3198, H8081, H7218): his rebuke is the finest oil, the anointing oil of a feast; al-yani roshi (H5106): let my head not refuse it. The verse contrasts with verse 4: better a friend's fist than an enemy's dinner. ki-od u-tephillati be-raotehem (H8605, H7451): the prayer keeps standing against their evils.

6.text: Their judges have been thrown down against the sides of the rock; then they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.
6.amp: When their judges [shaphat] are overthrown [shamat — let fall, hurled] in stony [sela — the crag] places ['by the hands of the rock', yad], they shall hear [shama] my words [emer]; for they are sweet [naam — pleasant].
6.notes: nishmetu bi-yede-sela shophetehem (H8058, H3027, H5553, H8199): their judges dropped down the rock's sides — the fate of the wicked rulers, as Jehu's officers threw Jezebel from the wall. ve-shameu amarai ki naemu (H8085, H561, H5276): then the people will hear David's words and find them sweet — the crowd listens once the tyrants are gone. The Hebrew of verses 6-7 is the hardest in the Psalter; this reading follows the KJV and WEB.

7.text: As when a man plows and splits open the ground, so our bones lie scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
7.amp: Our bones [etsem] are scattered [pazar] at the grave's [sheol] mouth [peh], as when one cuts [palach — cleaves, plows] and cleaves [baqa — splits] wood upon the earth [eretz].
7.notes: kemo pholeach u-boqea ba-aretz (H6398, H1234, H776): like a plowman splitting the ground — nipzeru atsamenu le-phi sheol (H6340, H6106, H6310, H7585): our bones scattered at Sheol's mouth, the way clods are turned up behind a plow. Whose bones — the psalmist's company, or the judges of verse 6 — the Hebrew does not settle; either way, the grave is at the door.

8.text: But my eyes are fixed on You, O GOD the Lord; in You I take refuge — do not leave my soul stripped bare.
8.amp: But mine eyes [ayin] are unto You, O GOD [YHWH] the Lord [Adonai]: in You is my trust [chasah — I take refuge]; leave [arah — pour out, strip] not my soul [nephesh] destitute ['make not my soul bare', arah, the KJV margin].
8.notes: ki elekha YHWH Adonai enai (H3069, H136, H5869): the Name written GOD in capitals, the KJV's signal for YHWH beside Adonai — eyes on Him, Psalm 123's posture. bekha chasiti (H2620): refuge taken; al-tear naphshi (H6168, H5315): arah is 'to pour out, to strip naked' — do not leave my soul emptied, exposed like a drained vessel.

9.text: Keep me out of the jaws of the trap they have laid for me, and from the snares of the workers of iniquity.
9.amp: Keep [shamar] me from the snares ['the hands of the snare', yad pach, the KJV sense] which they have laid [yaqosh — set as a fowler] for me, and the gins [moqesh — traps, baited snares] of the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven].
9.notes: shomreni mi-yede phach yaqeshu li (H8104, H3027, H6341, H3369): keep me from the HANDS of the trap — the pach is the fowler's spring-net, and yaqosh the fowler's verb — u-moqeshot poale aven (H4170, H6466, H205), the baited snares of the iniquity-workers. Psalm 91:3's fowler again.

10.text: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, all together, while I pass safely by.
10.amp: Let the wicked [rasha] fall [naphal] into their own nets [makmor], whilst that I withal [yachad — together, at the same time] escape ['pass over', abar, the KJV margin].
10.notes: yippelu be-makhmorav reshaim (H5307, H4364, H7563): the wicked into their own nets — Psalm 57:6's justice — yachad anokhi ad-eebor (H3162, H5674): 'together', all at once, while I pass over — abar, the crossing-verb. The evening ends with the psalmist walking past the sprung traps toward morning.
